items.stem: What is the correct containment order in OneNote?

options.text: Notebook contains sections, which contain pages
options.rationale: Correct: notebooks hold sections, which hold pages.

options.text: Page contains sections, which contain notebooks
Section contains notebooks, which contain pages
Everything is a single flat list

items.explanation: Correct: a notebook contains sections, and sections contain pages.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make OneNote content easier to find later? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Applying tags such as a to-do tag to action items
options.rationale: Correct: tags enable tag-based search and summaries.

options.text: Using consistent section and page names
options.rationale: Correct: consistent naming improves search and navigation.

options.text: Storing everything on one untitled page

options.rationale: Unsynced notebooks are not searchable across devices.

items.explanation: Correct: tags and consistent naming make content far easier to find later.

items.stem: For a OneNote notebook to be searchable and editable across your devices and shareable with others, it should be:

options.text: Stored and synced in OneDrive or SharePoint
options.rationale: Correct: cloud sync enables cross-device access and sharing.

options.text: Kept only on one local hard drive
options.rationale: A local-only notebook cannot sync or be shared.
Paper is neither searchable nor shareable digitally.
A screenshot is static and not the live notebook.

items.explanation: Correct: storing and syncing the notebook in OneDrive or SharePoint enables cross-device access and sharing.
